Structs let you create custom types that are meaningful for your domain. By using structs, you can keep associated pieces of data connected to each other and name each piece to make your code clear. In
blocks, you can define functions that are associated with your type, and methods are a kind of associated function that let you specify the behavior that instances of your structs have.
But structs aren’t the only way you can create custom types: Let’s turn to Rust’s enum feature to add another tool to your toolbox.
